summary.headline: HPL Electric FY26 revenue crossed Rs 1,800 crore; C&I grew 26% to Rs 784 crore and Q4 C&I hit a record Rs 214 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue crossed Rs 1,800 crore and Q4 revenue exceeded Rs 500 crore for the first time, with EBITDA growing ahead of revenue and gross margins improving. Consumer and Industrial (C&I) grew 26% to Rs 784 crore and rose to 43% of revenue from 37%, led by wires and cables (up 50% to Rs 340 crore). Smart metering recovered from an industry-wide execution disruption earlier in the year, with Q4 its strongest quarter, and the order book stood at over Rs 3,200 crore (over 97% metering) as of 22 May 2026. Management flagged C&I margin pressure in FY26 from mix shift and a lag in passing on commodity-linked price increases, which it expects to ease from late April and May.

financial_highlights.value: Above Rs 500 crore (first time crossing this level)

financial_highlights.change: up from 37% in FY26's prior year

financial_highlights.value: Over Rs 3,200 crore (metering over 97%) as of 22 May 2026

segments.name: Smart metering
segments.commentary: Q4 was the strongest metering quarter of FY26 after an industry-wide execution disruption earlier in the year; order book over Rs 3,200 crore as of 22 May 2026, with Q4 EBIT margin about 17.5%. Neeram Pulse smart water meter expected to add marginal revenue from H2 FY27, with meaningful revenue in 1-2 years.

segments.name: Consumer and Industrial (C&I)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 26% to Rs 784 crore in FY26; Q4 record Rs 214 crore. Wires and cables grew 50% to Rs 340 crore, largely volume-led (over 80% standalone growth in Q4), with switchgear, lighting and fans also contributing.

guidance_outlook: Management said C&I should cross Rs 1,000 crore revenue in FY27, though it normally would not give a specific number; described as a starting point to scale further over 3-5 years.

Smart metering demand viewed as intact; management believes the government's extended deadline (around March 2028) is achievable, and expects industry requirements of 31-32 crore meters over the next 4-5 years.
Industry volumes expected to reach roughly 18-20 crore meters installed over the next two years, with realisations declining as volumes rise.
FY27 capex expected to be mainly maintenance capex after substantial capex in FY26.
Debt expected to remain at current levels despite revenue growth; no immediate reduction planned.
C&I margins expected to recover as price increases passed on by end-April and early May, with commodity pressure easing.
capex_capacity: FY26 saw substantial capex, much of it in metering; FY27 capex expected mainly maintenance.
Capacity not a constraint for smart metering even if execution ramps up, per management.
Dedicated AMI water meter manufacturing facility inaugurated at Gurugram.
Promoter pledge of about 2.42% attributed to one promoter entity; management expects it to reduce in coming quarters and said it is not linked to capex.
demand_pricing: Smart metering: about 7 crore of roughly 22 crore sanctioned meters installed; about 15 crore tendered; balance 5-9 crore yet to be tendered by AMISPs. Company says it is a preferred vendor for almost every AMISP and is not directly bidding tenders.
Q1 FY27 metering dispatches tied to AMISP clearances; management sees demand intact and Q4 trend continuing into Q1.
Realisations in metering declining as tenders come in at lower prices, offset by volume growth; company says margins remain good.
C&I: channel expansion via 900+ authorised dealers and 85,000 retailers; a campaign pushes dealers to carry broader product baskets; BTL activity increased; new switch range launched in Patna.
C&I price increases in switchgear, lighting and fans taken mainly in Q1 FY27 with a 2-3 month lag to trade; first lighting price increase in about 7 years passed through.
Input cost pressure from metals, industrial plastics and crude since February; management sees some easing in the last week.

qa_highlights.question: Will C&I cross Rs 1,000 crore in FY27, and what is the metering demand trend into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is moving toward and should cross Rs 1,000 crore C&I revenue, with Q1 traction already visible. Metering demand is intact, with Q1 execution timing dependent on AMISP clearances.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Neeram Pulse revenue timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Marginal revenue expected from H2 FY27; BIS mark obtained, with other international certifications and pilots ongoing. Meaningful revenue in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to UP and state election slowdowns?
qa_highlights.answer: UP exposure is small, through one AMISP only. Some states may slow, but supply ramp-up is under way in West Bengal and five states are not in elections; meters can be reprogrammed for prepaid or postpaid from the backend.

qa_highlights.question: Gas meters and water meter TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: No gas meter plans yet, though internal studies are done. Water metering depends on state and municipal policy; tenders are out, and the company is new to the segment but believes its technology is superior.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration and Adani exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Supplies to GMR, Adani, IntelliSmart and other AMISPs; company claims it is a preferred vendor across almost all active AMISPs and declined to give exact shares. Management said it stopped detailed order announcements for competitive reasons.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the C&I margin decline and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix shift towards lower-margin wires and cables plus commodity-linked cost increases from February, passed on by end-April and early May. Management expects margins to recover.

qa_highlights.question: Debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt expected to stay at current levels as revenue grows; long-term debt was added after capex in the last 3 years, with no immediate reduction planned.

risks_watch: Smart metering execution pace and AMISP-level clearances driving quarterly dispatch timing.
Metering realisations declining as volumes scale and new tenders come at lower prices.
C&I margin recovery depends on pass-through of commodity-linked price increases, with a 2-3 month lag.
Customer concentration: sizeable exposure to a few large AMISPs; management did not disclose shares.
Promoter pledge of about 2.42%, expected to reduce.
Unproven new ventures (Neeram Pulse smart water meter, international metering) with approvals and utility adoption timing uncertain.
Fresh regulatory disclosure requirements for orders may limit visibility into order details.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order visibility, especially in C&I and smart metering, but noticeably hedged on specific numbers (declined to give exact C&I targets or AMISP shares) and cautious on water metering timing and near-term margin recovery.
